correctness.rationale: The final claim is explicitly restricted to two mirrored packets with a common positive-frequency L1 envelope H and fixed a,b>=0. Their disjoint Fourier supports have exact numerator ((a^2+b^2)/2) int_0^infty |Hhat(u)|^2/u du because omega(x)=2min(x,1-x). Carrier-phase averaging yields denominator M(a,b)^2 ||H||_1^2; the periodic averaging follows by L1 approximation. Hardy H1=H2 H2 factorization and the Cauchy-Schwarz convolution estimate give the sharp half-line Carleman quotient Q(H)<=1. The analytic H0(t)=(1-2 pi i t)^-2 has Fourier transform u exp(-u)1_{u>0}, norm 1/2 and weighted integral 1/4; positive-frequency cutoffs approximate it in L1. The phase average m(c) decreases strictly with c=2ab/(a²+b²), hence equal packet strengths uniquely maximize the amplitude factor at pi²/16. The global interval constant is only bounded between pi²/16 and 1. Independently checked sharp H0 integrals and amplitude inequalities for four amplitude pairs.
residual_risks: Half-line H1 factorization is a standard invoked theorem rather than reproved in the package. The unrestricted sharp interval constant remains undetermined.
